_what: Commits that are DIFFERENT commits but the SAME INSTRUMENT. C8 groups the board by instrument, not by commit sha; every commit listed under one instrument id is treated as that instrument. A commit absent from this file is its own instrument, which is the safe default: silence never merges anything.
_why: C8's claim is that one instrument measured every column, so the only thing differing between two columns is the gateway. The commit sha is a PROXY for the instrument, and it is a loose one in exactly one direction: a commit can change while the instrument does not (a gateway's own config, a test, a workflow). Failing those is a false positive that costs a full field re-run for no gain in truth. The proxy is never loose the other way, so this file can only ever excuse a difference the binaries prove is not there.
_evidence_rule: An entry is only admissible with BUILT-ARTIFACT evidence: build the shipped binaries at each commit and record their hashes. Identical bytes out of a reproducible build is proof, not argument. Do NOT add an entry reasoned from a diff - 'this looks test-only' is how a real instrument change gets waved through. If the binaries differ, the commits are different instruments and the field re-runs.

instruments.reason: The 14-box field ran on dd26a54. Plano failed to boot on it for two config reasons, and 8d74212 fixes plano's own config, corrects plano's matrix, adds tests, and wires an existing test into CI. Re-running the other thirteen to move a gateway config file would have changed no measurement.

evidence.method: cargo build --release --bin otb at each commit in a clean worktree, plus the mock-arm64 asset that bench-rig rebuilt from 8d74212, compared against the hash the running boxes recorded

instruments.reason: The 2026-08-02 field run landed across three commits because it was rebuilt in stages: seven gateways re-ran after a network event killed their orchestrator, busbar re-ran after its box hit the 8h cost cap mid-grid, and six re-ran to move off an engine whose record.rs genuinely differed. Nothing under engine/ changed between these three - the commits carry site, audit and gateway-manifest work - so re-running fourteen gateways to move those files would have changed no measurement.

evidence.method: cargo build --release --bin otb at each commit in a separate detached git worktree, same host and toolchain, hashed with shasum -a 256. Also verified pairwise that git diff engine/ between the three commits is empty - but the binaries are the admissible evidence, and the diff is only how the entry was found worth checking.

instruments.reason: busbar 1.5.0 measured at 80030c2f. The other thirteen were then re-measured PINNED to that same commit (BENCH_COMMIT=80030c2f) precisely so the board would be one instrument - and they came back stamped 7fd350ed, because run-on-ec2.sh derived the stamp from the operator's local HEAD instead of the commit the boxes fetch. They ran the pinned tree; only the label was wrong. 7fd350ed is 80030c2f plus one board commit (drop the 1.4.1 declaration, move a star record, add a snapshot) and touches no engine file. The stamping bug itself is fixed in the same change that adds this entry, so the two can no longer diverge; this entry exists because the artifacts on disk were already stamped by the broken path and re-running fourteen gateways to correct a label would change no measurement.

evidence.method: cargo build --release --bin otb at each commit in a separate detached git worktree, same host and toolchain, hashed with shasum -a 256. `git diff 80030c2f 7fd350ed -- engine/` is also empty, but the binaries are the admissible evidence and the diff is only what made the entry worth checking.
